content.prompt:
The diagram below shows how sheep's wool is processed to make knitting yarn.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

process_steps.label: Shearing
process_steps.description: Sheep are sheared once a year in spring, and each fleece is removed in a single piece.

process_steps.label: Sorting and grading
process_steps.description: Workers sort the fleeces by hand according to fibre length, fineness and colour.

process_steps.label: Scouring
process_steps.description: The wool is washed in tanks of warm water and detergent to remove grease, dirt and plant matter.

process_steps.label: Drying
process_steps.description: The clean wool is passed through hot-air dryers.

process_steps.label: Carding
process_steps.description: Rollers covered in fine wire teeth separate and straighten the fibres, which are then formed into a loose rope called a sliver.

process_steps.label: Spinning
process_steps.description: The sliver is stretched and twisted on spinning machines to produce a single strand of yarn.

process_steps.label: Plying
process_steps.description: Two or more single strands are twisted together to make a thicker, stronger yarn.

process_steps.label: Dyeing
process_steps.description: The yarn is coloured in heated dye vats, then rinsed and dried again.

process_steps.label: Winding and packing
process_steps.description: The finished yarn is wound into balls, labelled and packed for delivery to shops.

key_features: Overview: the process is linear, with nine stages that turn raw fleece on the farm into packaged yarn ready for sale.
The stages fall into three phases: preparing the raw wool (shearing, sorting, scouring and drying), making the yarn (carding, spinning and plying) and finishing (dyeing, winding and packing).
Early stages clean the wool: after hand-sorting by length, fineness and colour, it is washed in warm water and detergent and then dried with hot air.
Carding produces a sliver, which is spun into a single strand; strands are then plied together to make stronger yarn.
The yarn is dyed and dried a second time before being wound into balls, labelled and packed for shops.
